en.name: Maitake
en.summary: Maitake grows as a rosette of overlapping grey-brown fronds rather than a cap on a stem. No figure is published for it, so treat it like mushrooms generally: about 5–7 days refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, kept in a paper bag rather than plastic.
en.pantry: Maitake should not be kept at room temperature. Like any fungus it respires and sweats, and warmth softens the frond edges and starts the surface film that ends its life. There is no room-temperature figure and none should be assumed. Get it home and into the fridge, and take it out of any plastic wrapping on the way.
en.fridge: Keep maitake in a paper bag in the crisper at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, where about 5–7 days is the working limit — borrowed from the general figure for mushrooms, since nothing is published for maitake itself. Never store it sealed in plastic, which sweats it into slime within a day. It darkens and softens from the frond edges inward, so that is where to look. A whole cluster keeps noticeably better than torn pieces, so tear it apart only when you cook. Do not wash it; brush it clean instead.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline exists for maitake, so we do not give one. It can be torn into pieces and frozen raw in a flat sealed bag at −18 °C (0 °F) and cooked from frozen, and food held at that temperature stays safe indefinitely — but no quality window has been published. Drying is the more useful preservation route for this mushroom: dried maitake keeps for months and gives a deeper, more savoury stock than the fresh cluster does.
en.thawing: Cook maitake from frozen, straight into a hot dry pan. Thawed raw maitake releases a lot of water and will steam rather than brown, which loses the crisp edges that are the best part of it.
spoilage: A slimy or wet film across the fronds
Frond edges gone dark brown or black and soft
The cluster falling apart into mush at the base
A sour or ammonia smell instead of a clean, earthy, faintly peppery one
tips: Choose firm, dry clusters with springy fronds and no dark wet edges.
Keep the cluster whole and tear it apart only at the moment of cooking.
Roast or dry-fry it hard so the frond edges crisp — this is where maitake beats every other mushroom.

faq.q: How long does fresh maitake last in the fridge?
faq.a: About 5–7 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below in a paper bag. That figure is borrowed from mushrooms generally; none is published for maitake.
No timeline is published, so we do not give one. Torn pieces freeze raw at −18 °C (0 °F) and cook from frozen, but drying is a better preservation route for this mushroom.
No. It soaks up water readily and then refuses to brown. Brush the fronds clean and trim the base, which is where the grit is.

faq.q: Why should I keep the cluster whole?
faq.a: Every torn edge is a new surface losing water and picking up bacteria. A whole cluster keeps noticeably longer than the same mushroom pulled apart.

zh.name: 舞菇
zh.summary: 舞菇不是一般的傘柄狀菇，而是層層疊疊、呈灰褐色花簇狀的菌叢。它沒有公布的保存數據，可以比照菇類整體來看：4°C 以下冷藏約 5～7 天，裝紙袋而不是塑膠袋。
zh.pantry: 舞菇不應該放室溫。和所有真菌一樣，它會呼吸也會出水，溫度一高，葉狀菌蓋的邊緣就變軟，接著出現終結它的那層黏膜。這裡不提供常溫保存天數，也請不要自行推估。買回家盡快冷藏，路上就可以把塑膠包裝拆掉。
zh.fridge: 請裝進紙袋放在 4°C 以下的蔬果保鮮室，約 5～7 天是工作上限——這是比照菇類整體的數字而來，因為舞菇本身沒有公布的數據。絕對不要密封在塑膠袋裡，一天就能把它悶成黏糊。它是從菌葉邊緣往內變暗變軟的，判斷時就看那裡。整叢保存明顯比撕開的碎片耐放，所以請在要煮時才撕開。不要洗，用刷的清乾淨就好。
zh.freezer: 舞菇沒有公布的冷凍保存期限，所以我們不提供數字。它可以撕成小塊、平鋪裝密封袋生凍於 −18°C，使用時不解凍直接下鍋；食品在該溫度下安全上可無限期保存，只是沒有公布的品質期限。對這種菇來說，乾燥其實是更實用的保存方式：乾舞菇可以放好幾個月，而且熬出來的高湯比鮮菇更濃郁。
zh.thawing: 舞菇請不解凍直接下乾熱鍋。解凍過的生舞菇會大量出水，在鍋裡只會冒蒸氣而煎不上色，也就失去它最迷人的焦脆邊緣。
spoilage: 菌葉表面出現黏滑或濕答答的薄膜
菌葉邊緣轉成深褐或發黑並且變軟
整叢在基部散開變成糊狀
有酸味或阿摩尼亞味，而不是乾淨的土香與淡淡胡椒香
tips: 挑整叢結實乾爽、菌葉有彈性、邊緣沒有發暗濕爛的。
保持整叢完整，要煮的時候才撕開。
只能用紙袋，絕對不要密封塑膠袋。
用力烘烤或乾煎讓邊緣焦脆——這正是舞菇勝過其他菇類的地方。

faq.q: 鮮舞菇放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 4°C 以下冷藏、裝在紙袋裡約 5～7 天。這個數字是比照菇類整體而來；舞菇本身沒有公布的數據。
沒有公布的期限，所以我們不給數字。撕塊生凍於 −18°C 可以不解凍直接下鍋，但對舞菇來說乾燥是更好的保存方式。
不要。它很會吸水，吸飽之後就怎麼煎都不上色。用刷的把菌葉清乾淨，基部有土的地方削掉即可。
每一個撕開的斷面都是新的失水面和細菌入口。整叢保存會比同一朵撕碎的明顯耐放。
